items.summary: The opinions expressed here by Trellis expert contributors are their own, not those of Trellis or its editors .

items.title: US data centre demand growing ten times faster than grid capacity, research finds
items.summary: US data centre electricity demand has grown almost ten times faster than grid capacity over the past 25 years, with mounting power constraints delaying new developments and accelerating investment in alternative energy sources, according to new research.

items.title: Donors are falling short, but Indigenous communities are delivering
items.summary: As COP31 provides guidance on the world’s climate funds, Indigenous Peoples and local communities must define what counts and how impact is measured, argue Jonathan Jennings, co-chief executive of Health In Harmony and Minnie Degawan, managing director of the FSC Indigenous Foundation.

items.title: COP Covered podcast: Who pays? Finance day, a Trojan Horse and the case for investing in resilience
items.summary: The fifth episode of edie’s daily COP31 Covered podcast is streaming now, featuring an exclusive interview with Aviva’s Claudine Blamey on why resilience needs investment before disaster strikes.

items.title: COP31 at the halfway mark: What happened during week one?
items.summary: COP31 has reached its halfway point in Antalya, Türkiye, with negotiations set to continue into the second week as countries work towards an agreement on a final cover text.

items.title: WEBINAR ON THURSDAY: How to turn climate risk insights into adaptation action
items.summary: This webinar, held in partnership with SmartResilience on 19 November, will explore why and how leading organisations are moving from simply measuring risk to actively adapting in order to protect their operations, assets and supply chains.

items.title: From Guterres’ goodbye to a Trojan Horse protest: What happened on 13 November at COP31?
items.summary: From Guterres’ final COP address to a $15bn Chinese investment in Turkish renewables, Finance and Trade Day put the question of who pays for the transition firmly centre stage.

items.title: The climate transition isn’t stalling, but COP31 must focus on implementation as much as ambition
items.summary: As geopolitical tensions and economic pressures test the global net-zero transition, co-chair of the Taskforce on Net Zero Policy, Helena Viñes Fiestas, argues that COP31 must focus on turning commitments into action.

items.title: UK Government outlines steps for businesses to participate in voluntary carbon markets
items.summary: The Government has published a long-awaited response to a consultation on raising the integrity of voluntary carbon and nature market credits, outlining how it plans to support businesses that want to invest in carbon markets to help with value chain decarbonisation.

items.title: COP31: New UN framework puts businesses’ net-zero progress on public record
items.summary: The new Net-Zero Recognition Framework (NZRF) aims to make it easier for businesses, banks and cities to share their net-zero progress, enhancing transparency across the real economy.
